steps.title: Write a clear advert
points: Say what they will actually do
steps.tip: A specific advert gets fewer, better applications.

steps.title: Use an internship job board
points: Keep the advert live until you close
steps.tip: Pick boards built for students and graduates.

steps.title: Call university careers teams
points: Ask about job boards and mailing lists
Build a relationship for next year
steps.tip: One good careers contact can fill roles every year.

steps.title: Ask your own network
points: Ask staff to pass it on
steps.tip: Referrals often bring the most motivated applicants.

steps.title: Meet students at events
points: Book a stand at a careers fair
Give a short talk to a society
steps.tip: Ten minutes face to face beats a hundred cold emails.

steps.title: Make applying easy
points: Ask for a CV and a few short questions
Make it work on a phone
steps.tip: Long forms lose the best applicants first.

captions.linkedin:
Hiring an intern in London? Here are 6 places to find great applicants.

1. Write a clear advert: real tasks, must-have skills, dates and hours
2. Use an internship job board that students actually search
3. Call university careers teams (London has dozens)
4. Ask your own network and share it on LinkedIn
5. Meet students at careers fairs and society talks
6. Make applying easy, especially on a phone

Save this for your next hiring round.

Advertise your internship at internwise.co.uk/employers
